messages:
elaine (PM): Quick brain dump — Console wants a tiny canary UI that shows per-invocation econ for routes: token cost, cache savings, model-delta. Main question: how should we attribute shared prefetch/cache savings across routes? need a default we can show in the UI before we build full lineage. @samir any constraints on telemetry cost for a live preview?

samir (Eng): We should avoid heavy joins in the hot path. Telemetry is sampled today, so realtime per-invocation joins will be expensive. Proposal: deterministic sampling (e.g. 1% by hash) for the preview; store lightweight attribution metadata (fingerprint + fraction). For UI default: first-owner crediting + fallback to proportional split by token-length/promptshape. :thinking:

maria (SRE): From SRE POV we need latency context when surfacing cheaper routing — otherwise product folks will route traffic into a p95 regression. Show p50/p95 side-by-side with cost delta. Also request: preview must be stable for 24h windows to avoid noisy canary signals.

jordan (Analytics): For the initial prototype I can reuse existing sampled table. Example SQL I run to compute an amortized cache saving per-route (simplified):

```
SELECT
  route,
  SUM(prefetch_hits * model_unit_cost) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS amortized_prefetch_saving_per_invocation,
  AVG(token_count) AS avg_tokens
FROM sampled_invocations
WHERE event_time >= now() - interval '1 day'
GROUP BY route;
```

We can add `fingerprint_credit_fraction` to sampled_invocations to support proportional splits. Backfill is doable for last 7 days.

samir (Eng): For deterministic sampling use something like: `WHERE mod(hash_text(invocation_id), 100) < ${sample_rate}`. Keep sample_rate in config and expose it in the UI. Also: don't persist raw KV cache blobs — store `cache_fp` + `claimed_fraction` per invocation. That keeps storage small.

elaine (PM): UX Q: default toggle between "amortized" and "per-invocation" views? And an explain hover that says which attribution method is used (first-owner / proportional / manual). That should reduce bikeshedding.

costbot (bot): deploy-notice: econ-ingest v2.3 deployed (2026-03-21T02:12Z). Sampling default set to 1%. See https://internal.redwood/econ/deploys/2345 :robot_face:

maria (SRE): Can we also add an alert rule: if sampled cost delta between primary/cheaper route > 10% AND p95 latency diff > 200ms, open a canary blocker? Otherwise traffic shift automation might make things worse. :+1:

samir (Eng): Agreed. One more infra note: storing `cache_fp` + `fraction` allows us to reconstruct amortized savings offline without keeping per-token state. We can ship a backfill job that replays sampled events into the console indexes.

elaine (PM): Plan suggestion: I will scope a lightweight prototype: (1) UI card + toggle, (2) telemetry hook that flips `route_econ_preview=true` on canaries, (3) backend API to return sampled econ rows. Samir: can you own backend API and sampling config? Jordan: can you add the prototype analytics view (read-only) by next Thu? Maria: will you help define the alert thresholds?

jordan (Analytics): SGTM. I'll start the view and wire the SQL above; expect first PR by Wed EOD.

maria (SRE): Quick reminder: add GDPR flags for Private deployments so we don't persist any user prompt text in the sampled table. Store only fingerprints/lengths.

elaine (PM): thanks all — I'll write the RFC and the minimal acceptance criteria (canary traffic shows econ card, toggle exposes attribution method, and alerting fires on the rule). Scheduling sync tomorrow 10:30.
